newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary gas supply safe despite Gazprom freeze-MOL.
newsitem.headline: Hungary gas supply safe despite Gazprom freeze-MOL.

text.p: Hungary said on Thursday its gas supply is not in danger, despite the Russian government's freezing of $2.8 billion worth of assets belonging to Russian gas giant Gazprom, Hungary's main supplier.
"Hungary's gas supply is definitely in no danger," an official of oil and gas company MOL told Reuters.

Russia on Wednesday froze some of Gazprom's assets in an attempt to recoup $2.8 billion of unpaid taxes. Gazprom said it is owed more than three times that amount by consumers, which include the government.
Hungary imports 55 percent of its annual 11 billion cubic meters gas consumption, most of it from Russia.
MOL officials also said the company has two billion cubic meters of gas storage capacity and the remaining 45 percent of the consumption comes from domestic sources.
Germany's Ruhrgas on Monday started to supply Hungary with 0.5 billion cubic meters of natural gas per year, a move MOL said was the first step towards diversifying Hungary's gas sources.
The contract includes an agreement by which the German company will provide emergency backup in case of technical problems with eastern gas supplies.
